_: THE QUALIFICATION — what every WEC-LC learner receives, on every route.
This file is the part of the Master Plan that does not change with
price. It specifies the award and the academic work that produces it:
the curriculum, the assessment, the marking, the moderation and the
conferral. Every one of the five routes carries all of it, identically,
and that identity is the plan's first commercial fact — one academic
standard, several ways of reaching it.
Every leaf is { v: value, b: basis, s: source or reasoning, u: unit }.
Bases: design — a specification the College sets for itself; management —
a planning assumption, to be replaced by measurement once the College
operates; evidenced — a published external source; interim — a figure
the evidence sweep is to replace, and which the plan may not publish.
Built from zero: nothing here is read from the College's existing

levels.s: Six levels, A1 to C2 on the CEFR

levelNames.s: The six levels of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages

modulesPerLevel.s: Ten modules a level, each a unit of assessed study

termsPerYear.s: Three intakes a year: Spring, Summer, Autumn

monthsPerTerm.s: One level is studied across one four-month term

teachingWeeksPerTerm.s: Twelve teaching weeks in each term, the balance given to examination, moderation and conferral

quizzesPerLevel.s: One machine-marked quiz a module, low-stakes by design

assignmentsPerLevel.s: One assignment a module, marked by a person against a rubric published before the work

examinationsPerLevel.s: A three-hour written paper and a recorded spoken paper at the end of each level

secondMarkingShare.s: Every judged mark is read by a second marker before it reaches the candidate

reconciliationRate.s: Share of scripts on which the two readings differ by more than the three-point tolerance and a third reading is opened; replaced by the College's own marker-agreement record after the first two terms

reconciliationEffort.s: A third reading addresses only the disputed criteria, so costs less than a full first reading

resitRate.s: Share of candidates taking the one re-sit the regulations allow; a zero-revenue event that costs a new paper, a new sitting and a new double marking

candidatesPerInvigilator.s: Online invigilation, one invigilator to a sitting group

sittingHours.s: Three-hour paper plus admission and technical check

assignmentFirst.s: Minutes to mark one assignment by level — a C2 script is longer and harder to judge than an A1 script

writtenPaperFirst.s: Minutes to mark one written examination script, criterion by criterion

spokenPaperFirst.s: Minutes to mark one recorded spoken paper

moderationHoursPerLevelTerm.s: The moderation panel closes each level's batch each term within five working days, re-reading a sample

moderationSampleShare.s: A tenth of the batch is re-read in moderation

examinationBoardHoursPerTerm.s: The Examination Board sits once a term to confirm results and authorise conferral

paperVersionsPerLevelYear.s: A new paper each term, so that a re-sit never meets the paper it failed and no task is reused within a year

hoursPerPaperVersion.s: Authoring, rubric, trial marking and review of one paper version

curriculumMaintenanceHoursPerModuleYear.s: Annual revision of each module against what teaching and assessment show

qualityReviewHoursPerYear.s: The annual review cycle: curriculum, assessment, learner experience, teaching, standards, platform and outcomes

authoringHoursPerModule.s: Writing one module of assessed online study from nothing: learning materials, activities, quiz bank, assignment and rubric, review and accessibility check

levelAuthoredTermsAhead.s: Each level is authored and reviewed at least one full term before its first learners reach it
